text:
mira: Heads-up — after the preparse sidecar change landed, host ingress p99 jumped ~28% for small-chat workloads. Noticed it correlates with more gRPC small writes and extra parse passes.

jon: saw that too. do you have a flamegraph?

mira: attaching quick summary from local perf: main hotspots are: host preparse loop -> repeated `readv` wakeups, extra proto unpack in sidecar, and a new `KVCache` lock churn on miss paths. p50 unaffected, p95 up ~6%, p99 up ~28%.

alex: rough question — did the change add retries or buffer flushes on every chunk? that would create extra small writes on http2/grpc.

mira: yeah, we debounced at 1ms earlier, change removed debounce for simpler backpressure handling. code path: ingress -> preparse -> sidecar-unpack -> forward -> host tokenization.

ethan: omg that 1ms was doing more than we thought. we see more syscall rate and kernel-scheduler hops. small-write counts per request jumped by ~3x.

jon: can we try flipping the debounce back but keep the new parsing logic? quick canary with 0.8ms and 2ms thresholds.

mira: started a canary on a small hostpool with 2ms debounce. early numbers: syscall rate down 45%, p99 dropping ~18% (not all the way).

alex: likely still seeing KVCache lock thrash for partial parses. when sidecar returns small fragments, host tries to merge and updates cache metadata under the same mutex. we should switch to optimistic update + CAS.

ethan: agreed. plan: 1) reintroduce debounce (configurable), 2) make KVCache on partial-fragment updates use per-shard locks or CAS-fastpath, 3) add batching-hint that groups tiny requests into micro-batches at the ingress proxy.

mira: also seeing kernel selection regressions for short sequences — runtime picks a wide-kernel path assuming longer seqs based on older telemetry. after the preparse change, sequence-length distribution shifted left (more tiny requests). we should add a fast-path kernel selection based on a recent N-sample window (last 1s).

jon: that aligns with our performance model. short sequences should use narrow kernels and lower overhead. can we do a cheap histogram++ in ingress to inform kernel hint?

alex: yes, add a small LRU histogram in the host-proxy: increment counters for length bins, expose to runtime via tiny header `x-rw-kernel-hint: short|mixed|long`. runtime reads header and picks kernel.

mira: proof-of-concept patch in my branch. snippet: ```
# ingress micro-batcher pseudo
if seq_len <= 32 and microbatching_enabled:
  queue.append(req)
  if len(queue) >= 8 or time_since_first >= debounce_ms:
    flush_microbatch()
else:
  forward(req)
```

ethan: microbatching at ingress will help utilization but watch latency tail — we need to cap wait to 3ms max. also ensure streaming clients with client-side streaming keep low-latency path. add `cache-control: no-microbatch` opt-out.

alex: KVCache change idea: per-key sharded generation counter + CAS update for fragment merges. on miss, allocate new shard item without global lock. fallback path with global lock only for rare evictions. That should kill the hot mutex.

mira: wrote a quick microbenchmark: current merge path 120k mutex ops/s with 45% contention. CAS-shard approach reduces contention to <5% in simulated tiny-fragment load.

jon: amazing. timeline? can we land debounce revert + kernel-hint header as a quick fix, then follow with KVCache shard patch?

mira: will open two PRs: one for ingress debounce + kernel-hint header (hotfix), one for KVCache shard refactor (bigger).

ethan: how do we validate on canary? metrics to watch: p99 latency, small-write syscalls/sec, KVCache miss latency, kernel-path selection ratio. also check tokenization CPU burn (we might push tokenize into sidecar later).

mira: added a Grafana panel: ingress_small_writes/sec, host_p99_ms, kv_lock_wait_ms, kernel_choice_short_ratio. hooking up canary dashboard now.

deploy-bot: deploy started for canary cluster rw-ingress-canary-7 (mira/debounce-hotfix).

jon: after debounce hotfix on canary, p99 down 16% and small-write rate down 40% vs prod. good sign.

alex: let's run a 4h canary with mixed production traces. if stable, we roll to 20% traffic and add the kernel-hint header rollout.

ethan: one more note — streaming chunk coalescing: currently host treats every gRPC DATA frame as a parse boundary. coalescing small frames before parsing saved ~9% CPU in earlier experiments. put that in the ticket as follow-up.

mira: adding that to the follow-up list. tickets I'll file: RW-ING-237 debounce revert + config, RW-ING-238 kernel-hint header + ingress histogram, RW-RUNTIME-501 KVCache shard refactor, RW-ING-239 frame-coalesce optimization.

jon: thanks. small immediate wins, plus longer-term lock work. :thumbsup:

mira: cool — I'll post PR links when ready and ping for review.

alex: thanks — ping me for KVCache review, happy to help with microbench harness.

ethan: and I'll add canary monitors and an alarm for kernel-choice regression.

mira: closing loop — initial hotfix looks promising. continuing with KV and microbatch experiments.

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded for rw-ingress-canary-7 (mira/debounce-hotfix)
